entities.name: Orthopedic bedside manner concern
observations: Bedside manner or professionalism was the most frequent nonclinical complaint in orthopedic surgeon reviews: 65% in orthopedic oncology and 70% in hand-surgeon reviews.
Formal pediatric orthopedic complaints most often involved humanness, with communication central to most complaints.

entities.name: Orthopedic secondary concerns
observations: Wait time, limited consultation time, treatment-plan disagreement, and surgery or outcome concerns were reported but were less consistently dominant than interpersonal communication and bedside manner.
